sections.title: The letter eñe
paragraphs: The letter is named (eñe) /ˈeɲe/. It makes one main sound, which you hear in (niño) /ˈni.ɲo/, meaning boy, child. This letter has only one sound in Spanish.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Press the flat middle of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Send the air out through your nose. Keep your vocal cords vibrating so your voice stays on. You can place two fingers on the bridge of your nose to feel the vibration as air passes through.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: This letter always makes the sound /ɲ/ wherever it appears in a word. You can hear it in (año) /ˈa.ɲo/ and (España) /esˈpa.ɲa/. It never changes its sound before any vowel or consonant.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not pronounce this as two sounds like n and y in the English word canyon. Press the body of your tongue broadly against the roof of your mouth from the very start, so it stays as one single sound.
